title: AGING ACROSS
ECONOMIES
subtitle: Demographic Change, Regional Structure, and Age-Selective Migration
in Japan and the United States
takeaway: Shared population aging does not imply a single regional economic or demographic pattern.
layout: Three independent vertical columns; Key Findings immediately precedes Research Limitations, the final substantive block in Column 3.
research_limitations: Associations are descriptive, not causal. Population dates, GDP reporting periods, service-sector definitions, and migration measures differ across countries. ACS estimates carry sampling uncertainty; Japanese migration rates use rounded population denominators. Two association snapshots do not establish patterns in every year, and one year's migration flows cannot fully explain accumulated population age structure.
